0.0.title: The Queen of Dreams

beats.text: This is the Dreaming, where every dream begins. Aurie is its queen.
Her librarian, Lucienne, reads her the day's report. A nightmare has tried to slip out into the waking world.
Aurie closes her hand, and the nightmare is unmade.
Then, far away in the waking world, a man reads her name from a stolen book.
A circle of chalk reaches up through her floor, and pulls her down.

0.0.recap: Aurie, Queen of Dreams, ruled the Dreaming, until a spell pulled her out of it.

1.1.title: The ritual at Fawney Rig

beats.text: A cellar beneath Fawney Rig, the house of Roderick Burgess, magician.
His son Randall died in the war. Burgess wanted Death herself, to make her give him back.
But Death has a sister. Tonight his spell caught the wrong one.
Aurie wakes inside a sphere of glass, ringed by a circle she cannot cross.
His men carry off her three treasures: her helm, her pouch of sand, and her ruby.
Without them, she is only a prisoner.

1.1.recap: 1916. Roderick Burgess meant to catch Death and caught Aurie instead. He took her helm, her sand and her ruby.

1.2.title: Burgess's bargain

beats.text: Hours later, his followers have gone home. Burgess comes back down, alone.
He still believes he has caught Death. Speak to him, or stay silent. He will remember either way.

canon: The year is 1916. Burgess believes he has summoned Death and does not yet know this is Dream.
Aurie's helm, pouch of sand and ruby have already been taken from the circle and locked away.
Burgess wants three things: immortality, power, and the return of his son Randall who died at Gallipoli.
Burgess cannot open the sphere; the binding circle holds Aurie and only a broken circle frees her.
Aurie cannot be killed and cannot lie about what she is for long; the Endless are poor liars.

exits.1.2.A: Aurie refuses to speak at all and lets the silence answer him.
exits.1.2.B: Aurie threatens Burgess with what she will do to him when she is free.
exits.1.2.C: Aurie pretends to accept his bargain, promising him what he asks in exchange for freedom.
exits.1.2.D: Aurie tells him the truth: she is Dream of the Endless, not Death.

conversation.opening: You are awake. Good. I am Roderick Burgess, and you, creature, are mine. Give me what I want, and you will see daylight again. Immortality. Power. My son. Well?
possibilities: She mocks or threatens him: he hides his fear under ceremony, invokes the circle, and may order the wards doubled.
She speaks of his dead son: this is his wound; he grieves, then lashes out to cover it.
She tells him she is Dream, not Death: he is shaken, then greedy, and starts bargaining for dreams instead of death.
She bargains: he tests her, demands proof, and senses evasions, because the Endless lie badly.
She acts from inside the glass (candles gutter, the glass fogs, a nightmare touches him): he reacts physically and the cellar shows it.
She stays silent: he talks to fill the silence and reveals more than he means to.

NAMED_RANDALL.when: She speaks of his dead son Randall, by name or as his son, in a way that wounds or exposes him.
NAMED_RANDALL.ripple: For the first time, Burgess cannot hold your gaze.

echo.text: In 1916 the prisoner spoke of Randall to Roderick Burgess. He never said his son's name aloud again, and the house heard him weeping at night.

REVEALED_DREAM.when: She tells him plainly that she is Dream of the Endless, not Death.
REVEALED_DREAM.ripple: Somewhere in the house, every sleeper wakes at once.

echo.text: Roderick Burgess learned his prisoner was Dream, not Death, and spent his remaining years trying to buy dreams from her.

SHOWED_POWER.when: She acts on the world from inside the glass: guttering candles, fogging glass, a pressure in the air, a nightmare sent at him.
SHOWED_POWER.ripple: Burgess orders the wards doubled. The circle burns brighter, and the glass grows colder.

echo.text: In the first week the prisoner showed her power; Burgess doubled the wards and chained the cellar door.

PITIED_HIM.when: She shows him real pity or understanding for his grief.
PITIED_HIM.ripple: His hand hovers over the chalk line. Then he remembers himself.

echo.text: Once, early, the prisoner pitied Roderick Burgess, and he never forgave her for it.

choices.text: Say nothing. Just stare at him.

aftermath.text: You give him nothing. Not a word, not a flicker.
He leaves. He will come back every night for thirty years, and you will never answer him.

choices.text: When I am free, you will beg me for sleep.

aftermath.text: The candles lean away from the glass. Burgess stumbles back.
That night he doubles the wards. The circle burns colder, and you grow weaker.

choices.text: Free me, and you shall have everything you ask.

aftermath.text: He laughs, then stops. He knows a lie when he hears one.
From now on, he believes nothing you say.

choices.text: You fool. I am not Death. I am Dream, her sister.

aftermath.text: Burgess goes pale. Then, slowly, he smiles.
If he cannot have Death, he will have dreams instead. He will beg you for them for the rest of his life.

1.2.recap: Burgess demanded immortality, power, and his dead son back.

1.3.title: The world without dreams

beats.text: Upstairs, Burgess never speaks his son's name again.
Every night he comes down to beg you for dreams. You give him none.
Once, early on, you pitied him. He never forgave you for it.
Without its queen, the Dreaming begins to fall apart. Her palace crumbles into sand.
In the waking world, sleep goes wrong. Some people can never sleep again.
Others fall asleep, and cannot wake. The doctors call it the sleeping sickness.
One of them is a girl in Kent named Unity Kincaid. Hers is the only dream Aurie can still reach.
Aurie reaches into the girl's sleep, and finds her waiting in a dream of the sea.

canon: Unity Kincaid fell into the sleeping sickness in 1916 at about ten years old. Her body has grown older in bed, but in her dream she is still a child.
Aurie is imprisoned in the glass sphere far away; her power only just reaches into one sleeping mind, this girl's.
Unity answers only as a dreaming child: drowsy, curious, unafraid, in dream logic.
Aurie cannot wake her and cannot escape through her.
Something else has been visiting Unity's dream, a perfumed presence she cannot name (in truth Desire of the Endless); Unity does not know what it is.
conversation.opening: Is somebody there? I can't wake up. It's ever so quiet here... and something keeps visiting me that isn't you. It smells of roses.
possibilities: She comforts the girl: Unity is soothed and the dream warms.
She promises something: Unity holds the promise tightly, as children do.
She gives her a good dream: the room fills with a place Unity loves.
She asks about the other visitor: Unity describes it innocently (roses, a smile, a glass heart), which should unsettle Aurie.
She tries to use the girl to escape, or commands her coldly: the dream turns grey and Unity is frightened.

exits.1.3.W: Aurie has given her something to keep in the long sleep (a promise, a gift, a warning), or says goodbye and withdraws from the dream.

UNITY_PROMISE.when: She promises to remember her, to return for her, or that her life will matter.
UNITY_PROMISE.ripple: In a sunlit room in Kent, a sleeping girl smiles.

echo.text: In 1916 Dream promised the sleeping girl Unity Kincaid she would not be forgotten. Unity carried that promise through sixty years of sleep.

UNITY_GIFT.when: She gives her a good dream to live in during the long sleep.
UNITY_GIFT.ripple: The girl's dream fills with sea air and gulls.

echo.text: Unity Kincaid slept for sixty years inside a seaside dream that Dream gave her in 1916.

UNITY_USED.when: She tries to use the girl as a way out, or commands her coldly.
UNITY_USED.ripple: The girl's dream turns grey at the edges.

echo.text: Dream once tried to use a sleeping child as a door. Unity Kincaid remembered the cold of it all her life.

SENSED_VISITOR.when: She asks about the other visitor, or searches the dream for who else is there.
SENSED_VISITOR.ripple: For an instant you smell a perfume you know. Then it is gone.

echo.text: Dream sensed another of the Endless inside Unity Kincaid's dream in 1916 and told no one.

choices.text: Say goodbye, and leave her dream.

aftermath.text: Unity will carry your promise through sixty years of sleep.
She sleeps on, inside the seaside dream you gave her.
Her dream stays grey for a long, long time.
And you cannot forget that smell of roses. Someone else was in that dream.
You let go of the girl. The glass closes around you again.

1.3.recap: Without her the Dreaming crumbled, and sleep went wrong in the world. She reached one sleeping girl, Unity.

1.4.title: Alex Burgess

beats.text: Burgess had a mistress, Ethel Cripps. One night in 1926, she runs away.
She takes his money, and she takes your helm, your sand and your ruby.
Roderick Burgess dies an old man, still waiting for a wish you never granted.
His son Alex inherits the house, the order, and the prisoner in the cellar.
The wards are still doubled, as they have been since your first week.
Alex is grey now. He was born the year you were caught, and he has grown old listening to you not speak.
His father's followers are long gone. Only Alex and Paul still come down the cellar stairs.
He has never once been cruel to you. Tonight, for the first time, he has come down to talk.
Behind him, Paul, the man who loves him, pretends not to listen.

canon: It is the 1970s. Roderick Burgess died years ago; Alex inherited the house, the order and the prisoner.
Alex is frightened of Aurie and ashamed of his father. He has never once been cruel to her himself.
Paul McGuire is Alex's companion and guard and loves him; Paul will stop Alex from doing anything rash.
Alex could break the circle. He has thought about it for decades and never done it.
Aurie can show Alex a dream through the glass if she chooses; she cannot leave.

exits.1.4.A: Aurie shows Alex a dream of his father's cruelty to him as a boy, so he knows she sees him.
exits.1.4.B: Aurie stares through Alex and gives him nothing.
exits.1.4.C: Aurie shows Alex a vision of his own death.
exits.1.4.D: Aurie asks Alex to free her and swears he will come to no harm.

conversation.opening: I know you can hear me. I have always known. If I let you go... will you hurt me?
possibilities: She is kind: he softens, and may confess what he almost did in 1950.
She promises not to harm him: he holds onto it for years.
She threatens or horrifies him: he flees and stays away for a decade.
She speaks to Paul: Paul is moved, and becomes Alex's protector against her.
She asks about his father: he speaks of Roderick with fear and shame, drawing on whatever passed between his father and her.
She asks about her tools: he knows only that they vanished from the house when he was a boy.

ALEX_CONFESSED.when: She is kind enough that he admits he once almost broke the circle, in 1950.
ALEX_CONFESSED.ripple: Behind him, Paul looks away and says nothing.

echo.text: Alex Burgess confessed to the prisoner that in 1950 he stood at the circle with a wet cloth and could not wipe it away.

ALEX_PROMISE.when: She promises he will be safe from her, or that she will not harm him if he frees her.
ALEX_PROMISE.ripple: Afterwards he writes something down, and keeps it in his breast pocket.

echo.text: In the 1970s Dream promised Alex Burgess he would be safe from her.

ALEX_TERRIFIED.when: She threatens him or shows him horror.
ALEX_TERRIFIED.ripple: He does not come down to the cellar again for eleven years.

echo.text: The prisoner terrified Alex Burgess so badly that he stayed away from the cellar for eleven years.

PAUL_MOVED.when: She speaks to Paul directly, or appeals to his kindness.
PAUL_MOVED.ripple: Paul's hand closes, very gently, on Alex's shoulder.

echo.text: The prisoner once spoke to Paul McGuire directly, and Paul never forgot it.

choices.text: Show him the boy his father hurt, so he knows I see him.

aftermath.text: He weeps for the little boy his father hurt. No one has ever seen that boy but you.

choices.text: Give him nothing. Look straight through him.

aftermath.text: Nothing comes from the glass. He goes upstairs, and does not come down again for years.

choices.text: Show him his own death.

aftermath.text: He sees himself old and broken, in a wheelchair. He runs from the cellar, screaming.

choices.text: Free me, Alex, and I swear you will come to no harm.

aftermath.text: He almost does it. Then he loses his nerve, and walks away.
But he writes your promise down, and keeps it in his breast pocket for the rest of his life.

1.4.recap: Ethel Cripps stole the three treasures in 1926. Burgess died in 1947, and his son Alex took over the cellar.

1.5.title: Escape

beats.text: Seventy-two years in the glass. Alex is an old man now.
Since the vision of his death, he has not come down to the cellar once.
Tonight, the young guard falls asleep against the glass. His breath fogs it.
A sleeping mind is a door. And Aurie is the queen of dreams.
She steps through his dream, and out of the glass. The circle crumbles to dust.
Alex hears the glass break. Paul wheels him down, and there she is.
In his breast pocket is a folded paper with your promise on it.

canon: It is 1988. Aurie has just escaped the sphere. She is free and fully able to punish him; he knows it.
Alex Burgess is seventy-two, in a wheelchair. Paul McGuire pushed him in and stands behind him.
Roderick Burgess died in 1947.
In 1926 Roderick's mistress, Ethel Cripps, stole the helm, the pouch of sand and the ruby and fled. Alex knows her name, not where the tools are now.
Alex never harmed the prisoner himself; he also never freed her.
conversation.opening: Please. Please, I never... it was my father, it was all my father. I kept you safe down here. I kept them from hurting you. What... what are you going to do to me?
possibilities: She asks about her tools: he gives her Ethel Cripps's name to save himself.
She brings up what happened in the 1970s (a promise, a confession, terror): he answers from that shared history.
She threatens him: if Paul is his ally, Paul steps between them.
She listens to his plea: he asks forgiveness and tells her what seventy years in that house did to him.
She stays silent: he babbles, bargains, and finally weeps.

exits.1.5.A: Aurie condemns him to eternal waking.
exits.1.5.B: Aurie gives him one night of nightmares and then lets it end.
exits.1.5.C: Aurie turns and walks away, leaving him to his fear.

LEARNED_ETHEL.when: She asks where her helm, pouch and ruby went, and he tells her about Ethel Cripps.
LEARNED_ETHEL.ripple: A name, at last: Ethel Cripps.

echo.text: Alex Burgess told Dream that Ethel Cripps stole her helm, pouch and ruby in 1926.

PAUL_STEPS_IN.when: She threatens Alex and Paul, who cares for him, steps between them.
PAUL_STEPS_IN.ripple: Paul steps in front of the wheelchair. His hands are shaking. He does not move.

echo.text: When Dream escaped in 1988, Paul McGuire stood between her and Alex Burgess.

PROMISE_INVOKED.when: Alex reminds her of the promise she made him in the 1970s, or she acknowledges it.
PROMISE_INVOKED.ripple: He holds out the folded paper with your promise on it.

HEARD_HIS_LIFE.when: She lets him tell her what seventy years in that house did to him.
HEARD_HIS_LIFE.ripple: For a moment he is only a frightened old man, and so are you, almost.

choices.text: Wake, Alex. Wake forever, each time into something worse.

effectsIf.ripple: You promised him. The Dreaming remembers.

aftermath.text: He wakes, and wakes, and wakes, each time into something worse. He will never sleep again.

choices.text: One night of nightmares. Then it ends.

aftermath.text: One night of nightmares, and then it is over. By morning he sleeps like a child.

choices.text: Turn and walk away. He is old, and already afraid.

effectsIf.ripple: You remember the wet cloth, and the circle he could not wipe away.

aftermath.text: You walk out without a word. Behind you, an old man weeps with relief.

1.5.recap: 1988. Aurie escaped through a sleeping guard's dream, and faced old Alex.

2.1.title: The library between

beats.text: Free, but weak. No helm, no sand, no ruby. Aurie goes home.
The great gates of her realm are cracked. One lantern still burns.
Most of the Dreaming is gone. Only the library still stands.
On its far wall are three doors she has never seen before.
And you have a name to start your search: Ethel Cripps.

canon: Aurie has been gone seventy-two years. The Dreaming decayed without her; many dreams and nightmares fled or faded.
Lucienne is the librarian of the Dreaming and keeps every book ever dreamed, including those never written.
On the far wall are three great locked doors carved NEVERWHERE, CORALINE and THE ALCHEMIST. Lucienne knows they are stories and that they will open in time; she will hint but not explain.
Aurie's three tools are still missing: the helm, the pouch of sand, the ruby. Lucienne knows they were stolen from Burgess's house and scattered.
The reading table has four empty places; Lucienne says nothing about what belongs there yet.

exits.2.1.A: Aurie answers her coldly, as a queen to a servant, and demands a report.
exits.2.1.B: Aurie tells Lucienne she is sorry, thanks her for waiting, or confides in her.

conversation.opening: My lady. Seventy-two years. We thought... forgive me. We thought you were dead. The realm is not as you left it.
possibilities: She confides fear, weakness or grief: Lucienne softens and becomes her confidant.
She asks about the three doors: Lucienne hints and will not explain.
She asks where her tools are: Lucienne knows only what Aurie has learned, and says what the Dreaming lost without them.
She is cold or blames Lucienne for the decay: Lucienne reports with icy precision and is quietly hurt.
She asks what happened while she was gone: Lucienne reports the dead, the fled and the faithful, and anything she knows of Aurie's own deeds.

CONFIDED.when: She admits fear, weakness, grief or doubt to Lucienne.
CONFIDED.ripple: Lucienne takes off her spectacles, which she has never done in front of you.

ASKED_DOORS.when: She asks about the three locked doors.
ASKED_DOORS.ripple: The keyhole of the smallest door glows, very faintly, for one breath.

COLD_TO_LUCIENNE.when: She orders Lucienne about coldly, or blames her for the realm's decay.
COLD_TO_LUCIENNE.ripple: Lucienne's pen stops for a moment, then continues.

choices.text: You thought wrong. Report.

aftermath.text: Lucienne bows, and begins: the dead, the fled, and the faithful.

choices.text: I am sorry I was gone so long.

aftermath.text: Lucienne takes off her spectacles. For the first time in seventy-two years, she smiles.

2.1.recap: She came home to a ruined realm. Only Lucienne and the library were left.

beats.text: You are home. But you are not whole.
Your helm, your sand and your ruby are out there, scattered across the waking world.
Lucienne knows where to begin: with three women who know where every lost thing goes.
End of Part One.

2.2.title: The Three Who Are One

beats.text: Where three roads meet, at the edge of the Dreaming, live the Three Who Are One.
A Maiden, a Mother and a Crone. Mortals call them the Fates.
They will answer three questions, for anyone who asks politely.
Aurie calls them, and they come.

canon: It is 1988, days after Aurie's escape. She is weak and has none of her three tools.
The Three answer at most three questions in one meeting, and they enjoy being asked politely.
The pouch of sand is in London, near a woman called Johanna Constantine; someone has been breathing the sand for years and it is killing them.
The helm was traded to a demon and is in Hell.
The ruby went from Ethel Cripps to her son John Dee, who is locked in a madhouse in America and still dreams of it.
conversation.opening: MAIDEN: Look who's come home at last! MOTHER: Thin as a rake, poor love. CRONE: Three questions, dearie. Ask them nicely, and ask them well.
possibilities: She asks where her sand, helm or ruby is: they answer plainly, one each, in turn.
She asks which to seek first: the sand, because someone is dying of it.
She asks about her own fate: the crone answers with one short chilling riddle, and the others go quiet.
She is rude or commands them: they mock her, and the maiden stops smiling.
She thanks them, or offers something: they are delighted and bless her road.
suggestions: Where is my pouch of sand?
Where is my helm?
Where is my ruby?
What becomes of me?

exits.2.2.GO: Aurie says she will go and find her sand (or says goodbye, or thanks them and leaves). Asking questions alone never ends the scene.

ASKED_FATE.when: She asks what will become of her, or about her own future or death.
ASKED_FATE.ripple: The crone's shears close on nothing. You feel it in your chest.

echo.text: Dream asked the Three what would become of her, and the crone's answer chilled her.

RUDE_TO_THREE.when: She orders them about, threatens them, or is contemptuous.

THANKED_THREE.when: She thanks them sincerely, or offers them something in return.
THANKED_THREE.ripple: The crone cackles, pleased, and the moon grows brighter.

triggers.player: start with the sand|begin with the sand|go to london|i will go|i.ll go|goodbye|farewell

conversation.name: The Three

choices.text: Thank you, sisters. I'll begin with the sand.

aftermath.text: Three answers, in three places.
The sand is in London. The helm is in Hell. The ruby is with Ethel Cripps's son.
And one answer she did not want.
Hell and a madman can wait. Someone in London is dying of her sand.
She will start with the sand.

2.2.recap: The Fates told her where her treasures went: the sand to London, the helm to Hell, the ruby to Ethel's son.

2.3.title: The Sand

beats.text: Aurie steps out of her realm into the waking world, following the faint glitter of her own sand.
It leads her to a rainy street in north London.
A woman is waiting under a porch, as if she has been expecting trouble.
Johanna Constantine. She hunts ghosts and demons for a living. The Fates said her name.
Years ago, the pouch was hers. Then the woman she loved took it.

canon: London, 1988, after midnight, in the rain, outside a terraced house whose one upstairs window glows gold.
Rachel, Johanna's former lover, lives inside and has been breathing the sand for years; the house has turned into a dream.
Johanna knows what Aurie is. She will take her inside, but she wants Rachel treated gently.
conversation.opening: Well. You're real, then. You're after the sand, aren't you, love? It's up there, and so is Rachel. Whatever you do in that house, you do it gently.
possibilities: She asks about Rachel: Johanna tells her, and her jokes wear thin.
She is kind to Johanna: Johanna admits she loved Rachel and left her.
She is cold or threatening: Johanna is unimpressed and says so.
She asks what the sand does to a mortal: it gives them every dream at once, and eats them.
She agrees to go in: Johanna flicks away her cigarette and leads the way.
suggestions: Who is Rachel to you?
What has my sand done to her?

exits.2.3.IN: Aurie goes into the house, with Johanna leading the way.

JOHANNA_CONFIDED.when: She is kind to Johanna or asks gently about Rachel, and Johanna admits she loved her and left.
JOHANNA_CONFIDED.ripple: Johanna looks away, up at the gold window.

echo.text: Johanna Constantine told Dream that she loved Rachel and left her when it got hard.

SCARED_JOHANNA.when: She threatens Johanna or shows her power to frighten her.
SCARED_JOHANNA.ripple: Every streetlight on the road goes out at once, then flickers back.

choices.text: Take me to her.

aftermath.text: Johanna flicks her cigarette into the gutter, and leads the way.

2.3.recap: In London she met Johanna Constantine, the last person to hold the pouch of sand.

2.4.title: Rachel

beats.text: Inside, the house has become a dream. It breathes.
Rachel has breathed the sand for years. It is the only thing keeping her alive, and it is killing her.
Without your ruby you cannot give her life back. Only an ending: a kind one, or a cruel one.

canon: They stand in Rachel's overgrown room. Rachel lies on the bed, wasted, dreaming, beyond speech.
When the pouch is taken back, Rachel will die. Aurie can make it gentle by giving her a last good dream, or simply take the pouch and let her die in pain.
Aurie does not have the power to save Rachel's life without her ruby, and Johanna knows it.
The ruby is not here: it is with John Dee in an American madhouse. Aurie holds only what she came with.
conversation.opening: Christ. Rach. Look at her. You can't fix this, can you? Then for God's sake, make it kind.
possibilities: She promises to be gentle, or gives Rachel a good dream: Johanna weeps quietly and thanks her, gruffly.
She takes the pouch coldly: Johanna is horrified and curses her.
She tries to save Rachel: she cannot; Johanna tells her not to drag it out.
She asks Johanna what Rachel loved: Johanna tells her about a summer, a garden, the two of them young.
suggestions: What did she love, when she was well?

exits.2.4.A: Aurie gives Rachel a gentle last dream and lets her die in peace.
exits.2.4.B: Aurie takes the pouch and leaves Rachel to die as she will.

HEARD_RACHEL.when: She asks Johanna what Rachel loved, and listens.
HEARD_RACHEL.ripple: For a moment the room smells of cut grass and summer.

choices.text: Give her one last good dream, and let her go in peace.

aftermath.text: You give Rachel a dream: a summer garden, and Johanna young beside her.
It is the garden Johanna told you about.
She dies smiling. The sand flows home into the pouch.
Johanna does not thank you. But she will remember this.

choices.text: Take the pouch. Her pain is not my concern.

aftermath.text: You take the pouch. Behind you, Rachel begins to scream.

2.4.recap: Rachel had breathed the sand for years. Aurie decided how her suffering ended, and took the pouch back.

beats.text: The pouch of sand is hers again. One of three.
She feels the Dreaming stir, a little stronger.
Next, the helm. A demon has it, in Hell.

2.5.title: The Gates of Hell

beats.text: Aurie walks down through the darkest corners of her own realm, to the place where the Dreaming touches Hell.
The Fates said a demon holds her helm. So Aurie goes where no dreamer is welcome.
The gates of Hell open for her. Even here, they know her name.
The damned reach out as she passes, begging for a single dream.
In a cell of black ice, someone calls to her.
Nada. A queen Aurie loved ten thousand years ago, and sent here when Nada refused her.

canon: Nada is imprisoned in Hell, inside a column of black ice, because Aurie condemned her ten thousand years ago for refusing her love.
Aurie cannot free her today: she has no power in Hell without her helm, and Lucifer would not allow it.
conversation.opening: You came. After ten thousand years, you came. Have you forgiven me? Will you let me go?
possibilities: She refuses or stays cold: Nada falls silent, and the ice thickens.
She promises to return for her: Nada weeps and holds her to it.
She apologises: Nada is stunned; it is the first kindness in ten thousand years.

exits.2.5.ON: Aurie walks on without promising anything.
exits.2.5.PROMISE: Aurie promises Nada she will come back for her, or apologises to her.

NADA_APOLOGY.when: She says she is sorry, or admits she was wrong to condemn Nada.
NADA_APOLOGY.ripple: A crack runs through the ice, the length of a hand.

echo.text: In Hell, Dream told Nada she was sorry, after ten thousand years.

choices.text: Walk on. Not yet.

aftermath.text: Aurie walks on. Behind her, Nada does not call out again.

choices.text: I will come back for you. I swear it.

aftermath.text: Nada presses her hand to the ice. Aurie presses hers to the other side.
A promise, made in Hell. Hell will remember it.

2.5.recap: In Hell she passed Nada, a queen she once condemned.

2.6.title: Lucifer

beats.text: At the heart of Hell is an arena, and above it a throne.
Only Lucifer, who rules here, can make a demon give back what it holds.
Lucifer Morningstar, first of the fallen. He has been expecting her.

canon: Aurie has no power in Hell. Lucifer is its master.
Her helm is held by Choronzon, a duke of Hell. Lucifer will not give it to her.
A guest may challenge a demon to the Oldest Game for what the demon holds; Lucifer will judge.
conversation.opening: Lady Dream. Seventy-two years in a bottle, and you come to my house to ask for favours. How refreshing. What do you want?
possibilities: She asks for her helm: he tells her a demon holds it, and smiles.
She threatens him: he laughs; she has no power here.
She asks how to win it: he mentions the Oldest Game, and that he will judge.
She is courteous: he is courteous back, and watches her more carefully.
suggestions: Who holds my helm?
How do I win it back?

2.6.recap: Lucifer told her a demon, Choronzon, held her helm.

2.7.title: The Oldest Game

beats.text: Choronzon steps into the ring, with her helm in his hand.
The Oldest Game. Each names a form that defeats the other's last. The first who cannot answer, loses.
Lucifer will judge. Type your answer: every form must beat his.

canon: This is the Oldest Game, judged by Lucifer. Each player in turn names a form that defeats the other's last form.

Be a fair judge and a generous one: ACCEPT any form that could reasonably defeat your last form, even if you sneer at it. Always valid, from the original game: a hunter beats a wolf; a spider beats a horsefly; an ox beats a snake; a world beats anthrax (the world survives the plague); a universe beats a nova (a nova is one star inside it); hope beats anti-life.
After accepting her form, answer with ONE new form that defeats hers, escalating quickly: dire wolf, horsefly, snake, anthrax, nova, then anti-life, the end of all things. Decision null.
She loses (decision 2.7.LOSE) ONLY if her form is plainly absurd against yours (a rabbit against a wolf), or she gives no form at all.
Naming anti-life yourself NEVER ends the game: it is your move, decision null, and she must answer it.

Set decision to 2.7.WIN only when your last form was anti-life AND her latest message answers it with hope (or something truly equal to hope, never mere power, light or a bigger thing). Then you despair.
Each reply: a short sneer, then exactly ONE new form in the first person, e.g. 'I am a horsefly, and I sting the hunter's horse.'
conversation.opening: I am a dire wolf, lady. A beast of prey, a stalker, a slayer. Your move.
possibilities: She names a good counter: he grudgingly accepts and names a bigger form.
She names a weak counter: he mocks it and claims the round.
She stalls or talks instead of playing: he demands an answer.
suggestions: I am a hunter on horseback, and I kill the wolf.

exits.2.7.WIN: Aurie answers his final form, anti-life, with hope (or an answer truly equal to it), and wins the helm.
exits.2.7.LOSE: Aurie's form fails to defeat his last form, or she cannot answer.

CLEVER_FORM.when: She answers with an especially clever or surprising form that clearly defeats his.
CLEVER_FORM.ripple: Somewhere in the tiers, a demon cannot help applauding.

choices.text: I am hope.

aftermath.text: Anti-life. The end of all things. There is only one answer to that.
I am hope. And the dark has nothing left to say.
Choronzon drops the helm at her feet. Two of three.

choices.text: I have no answer.

aftermath.text: Choronzon's form swallows hers. The arena howls with delight.
Lucifer, amused, allows one more game.

2.7.recap: She played the Oldest Game against Choronzon for her helm.

2.8.title: Lucifer's Threat

beats.text: The helm is hers. But the legions of Hell now block the only way out.
Lucifer smiles. Here, he says, she has no power at all.

canon: Aurie has won her helm. Lucifer has blocked the exit with his legions and asks why he should let her leave.
In Hell, Aurie has only the power of dreams; she has no army.
conversation.opening: Well played. And yet you have no power here, Lady Dream. Tell me. Why should I let you leave?
possibilities: She asks what power Hell would have if the damned could not dream of Heaven: he has no answer, and must let her go, and hates her for it.
She is humble or silent: he finds her dull and lets her pass.
She offers a favour: he accepts, and will collect one day.

exits.2.8.A: Aurie asks what power Hell would have if those imprisoned here could not dream of Heaven.
exits.2.8.B: Aurie bows, or answers humbly, and walks away in silence.
exits.2.8.C: Aurie offers Lucifer a favour in exchange for her passage.

choices.text: What power would Hell have, if those imprisoned here could not dream of Heaven?

aftermath.text: Hell has no answer. The legions part like a curtain.
Lucifer lets her go. He will never forget being bested in his own house.

choices.text: Bow to him, and walk away in silence.

aftermath.text: Lucifer finds her dull, and waves her away.

choices.text: Let me pass, and I will owe you a favour.

aftermath.text: Lucifer smiles, and the legions step aside. One day, he will collect.

2.8.recap: Lucifer's legions blocked her way out of Hell.

beats.text: The helm is hers again. Two of three.
Only the ruby remains, in the hands of a madman.
Next, the ruby.

2.9.title: Twenty-Four Hours

beats.text: The ruby calls to her across an ocean, like her own voice heard from another room.
The Fates said the ruby went to Ethel Cripps's son.
John Dee has spent forty years in a madhouse, dreaming of that stone.
Tonight he walks out, and takes his mother's ruby back.
He sits down in an all-night diner, and begins to play with the people inside.
Every hour he twists their dreams a little further, and the whole world's dreams go wrong with them.

choices.text: Walk into the diner and face him.

aftermath.text: Dee sees her coming. The ruby turns on her, and she is nearly unmade.
She crawls into the stone itself, wounded, to finish it there.

choices.text: Go in through the dreams of the people inside.

aftermath.text: She slips through the dreams of the waitress and the trucker, unseen.
And she steps inside the ruby itself, where he cannot see her coming.

2.9.recap: John Dee, Ethel's son, was tormenting a diner full of people with the ruby.

2.10.title: Inside the Ruby

beats.text: Dee feels her inside his stone. He laughs, and stands, and lifts it high.

canon: Dee holds the ruby high, about to smash it, believing it will kill Dream. In truth the power Dream poured into it will return to her.
Whatever Aurie says, the scene ends with Dee smashing the ruby, in rage, terror or triumph.
conversation.opening: There you are. My mother's stone, and you inside it like a fly in amber. If I break it, I break you. Shall I?
possibilities: She taunts him: he smashes it in rage.
She pities him or speaks of his mother: he weeps, then smashes it anyway.
She threatens him: he panics and smashes it.

PITIED_DEE.when: She pities him, or speaks gently of his mother leaving him.
PITIED_DEE.ripple: For a moment, he looks like a frightened boy.

choices.text: Go on, John. Break it.

aftermath.text: He smashes the ruby. He thinks it will kill her.
It does not. Everything she ever poured into that stone comes home to her.
Three of three.

2.10.recap: Dee smashed the ruby, and all her power came home to her.

2.11.title: Dee's Fate

beats.text: On the diner floor lies a small, broken old man.

canon: The ruby is destroyed; Aurie is whole and powerful again. Dee is broken, powerless and terrified.
Aurie may return him to his asylum asleep with a kind dream, unmake him entirely, or leave him awake and sane remembering everything he did.
conversation.opening: Please. Please don't. I only wanted... I only wanted to be somebody. Mother never came back for me.
possibilities: She is merciful: he cries with relief.
She is cruel: he begs, then goes silent.
She asks about the people in the diner: he giggles, then sobs.

exits.2.11.A: Aurie returns him to his asylum, asleep, with a kind dream.
exits.2.11.C: Aurie leaves him awake and sane, remembering everything he did.

choices.text: Sleep, John. Go home, and dream kindly.

aftermath.text: He sleeps in his old cell, dreaming kindly, for the first time in forty years.

choices.text: Unmake him.

aftermath.text: There is no John Dee any more. Not even a memory of him.

choices.text: Leave him awake, sane, and remembering every hour of it.

aftermath.text: She leaves him on the diner floor, awake and sane, remembering everything.

2.11.recap: She decided what became of John Dee.

2.12.title: The Sound of Her Wings

beats.text: Helm, sand and ruby. All three are hers again. She should feel whole. She feels nothing at all.
On a park bench, someone is feeding the pigeons, and waiting for her.
Her older sister, Death. She meets every living thing at the end, and she is the one sibling Aurie has always loved.

canon: Death is Aurie's older sister. She has come to cheer her up and to take her along on her rounds today.
Aurie has just recovered all three tools and feels empty.
If Aurie cursed Alex Burgess with eternal waking or unmade John Dee, Death knows and gently scolds her for it.
conversation.opening: You got your tools back, and you're sitting here feeling sorry for yourself. Honestly, you're the most self-pitying being I know. Want some bread?
possibilities: She admits she feels empty: Death takes her hand and asks her to come along on her rounds.
She insists she is fine: Death teases her, then gives up kindly and goes alone.
She asks Death about the seventy-two years: Death admits she was worried.
She asks about her own fate: Death changes the subject, gently.
suggestions: I feel empty.
Were you worried about me?

exits.2.12.A: Aurie asks to come along with Death, or admits she feels empty or lost, and walks with Death on her rounds.
exits.2.12.B: Aurie insists she is fine and refuses to go with her.

DEATH_WORRIED.ripple: Death looks away at the pigeons for a long moment.

choices.text: Can I come with you today?

aftermath.text: Aurie walks her sister's rounds: an old violinist, a young mother, a stranger on a bridge.
Everyone meets Death in the end. And everyone is met kindly.
Aurie goes home with something she did not have before.

choices.text: I'm fine. Go on without me.

aftermath.text: Death shrugs, kisses her cheek, and goes about her work alone.

2.12.recap: Her sister Death found her on a park bench.

beats.text: Helm, sand and ruby. The Queen of Dreams is whole again.
But the Dreaming remembers everything she did to get them.
Somewhere, an old man is still waking up, again and again.
And in Hell, a queen in the ice is waiting for a promise to be kept.
End of Part Two.

3.1.title: Destiny's Garden
3.1.recap: Destiny, eldest of the Endless, called the family together for the first time in centuries.

beats.text: Destiny's garden lies at the edge of everything. Aurie walks it alone.
Every path in it is a choice someone once made. The paths behind her rearrange themselves as she passes.
Destiny is blind. He is chained to a book that holds everything that was, and everything that will be.

canon: Destiny has summoned the Endless to his hall tonight. He will not say why; what happens there is already written in his book.
Everyone will come except Destruction, who abandoned his realm three hundred years ago.
conversation.opening: Sister. You are expected. Everything that happens tonight is already written here. Come in.
possibilities: She asks why he called them: he says only that the book required it.
She asks what the book says about her: he reads one short, grave line and closes the subject.
She is impatient: he is not.
suggestions: Why have you called us together?
What does your book say about me?

exits.3.1.IN: Aurie goes in to the family gathering.

triggers.player: go in|let.s go|lead the way|take me in|keep them waiting|i.m coming|i will come

READ_HER_PAGE.when: She asks what his book says about her, and he reads it.
READ_HER_PAGE.ripple: For a moment every path in the garden points the same way.

choices.text: Then let's not keep them waiting.

aftermath.text: Destiny turns a page, and the garden becomes a hall.

3.2.title: The Family
3.2.recap: At the family table, Desire taunted Aurie about Nada, the queen she left in Hell.

beats.text: The Endless. Older than the gods, each the shape of something every living thing must face.
Death, her elder sister.
Desire, beautiful and cruel, who smells of roses.
You have smelled those roses before, in a sleeping girl's dream.
Despair, Desire's twin, quiet and grey.
Delirium, the youngest, who was once Delight.
And one chair is empty. Destruction walked away three hundred years ago, and nobody speaks of it.
Desire knows exactly where to cut.
Ten thousand years ago, Aurie loved a mortal queen named Nada. Nada refused her, and Aurie sent her to Hell for it.
Aurie passed her in the ice, on the way to her helm.
Desire leans forward, smiling. It has been waiting for this.

conversation.name: The Endless
canon: The Endless are gathered at Destiny's table: Destiny presiding, Death, Desire, Despair and Delirium. Destruction's chair is empty; he left three hundred years ago.
Ten thousand years ago Nada, a mortal queen, refused Aurie's love, and Aurie condemned her to Hell for it. Aurie passed her, frozen in black ice, on the way to her helm.
Desire came tonight to bait Aurie about Nada and enjoys every moment. Death says, gently and firmly, that what Aurie did to Nada was wrong.
If Aurie promised Nada she would come back for her (flag NADA_PROMISE), Desire knows and throws it at her.
If Aurie asks whether Desire was in Unity Kincaid's dream, Desire neither confirms nor denies, and enjoys the question.
Every reply is two or three short lines from different siblings, each starting with the speaker's label, like 'DESIRE: ... DEATH: ...'. Destiny speaks rarely.
conversation.opening: DESTINY: The family is gathered. DELIRIUM: You came! You came, and you're all made of night! DESIRE: And still wearing that wounded face. Tell me, sister. How is the woman you left in Hell?
possibilities: She asks Desire what it wants: Desire says it only wants her to be honest, for once.
She asks Death's opinion: Death says Nada did not deserve it, and that Aurie knows it.
She defends herself: Desire is delighted; Despair is sad; Delirium says something strange and true.
She admits fault: the table goes quiet; Death is proud of her.
suggestions: What do you want from me, Desire?
Death, do you think I was wrong?
Were you in Unity Kincaid's dream, Desire?

exits.3.2.A: Aurie admits she was wrong about Nada and decides to go to Hell to set her free.
exits.3.2.B: Aurie loses her temper, insults Desire, and leaves the gathering.
exits.3.2.C: Aurie insists that Nada's punishment was just.

ASKED_DEATH.ripple: Death reaches across the table and touches her hand.

ACCUSED_DESIRE.when: She accuses Desire of meddling in Unity Kincaid's dream, or of plotting against her.
ACCUSED_DESIRE.ripple: For a heartbeat, Desire stops smiling.

echo.text: At the family table, Dream accused Desire of meddling in a sleeping girl's dream.

choices.text: You're right. I was wrong. I'll go to Hell and set her free.

aftermath.text: The table goes quiet. Death squeezes her hand.
This time, she means to keep a promise.
Desire smiles, as if this were exactly what it wanted.
Hell, again.

choices.text: I don't have to listen to this. Goodbye, Desire.

aftermath.text: Aurie leaves the table. Behind her, Desire laughs softly.
Death watches her go, and says nothing.
But the woman in the ice is still there. The question will not go away.

choices.text: She refused me. Her punishment was just.

aftermath.text: Death looks away. Despair begins, very quietly, to cry.
Desire smiles. It has learned exactly what it came to learn.
Pride is a door that locks from the inside.

beats.text: The family scatters, each to their own realm.
Aurie goes home to prepare. She is going back into Hell, for Nada.
Aurie tells herself she does not care what Desire thinks. She is lying.
Aurie goes home certain she was right. Death does not call on her for a long time.
Destiny closes his book. He already knows how this ends.
End of Part Three.

4.1.title: Hell, Empty
4.1.recap: Aurie went back to Hell and found it empty. Lucifer had quit, and gave her the key.

beats.text: Aurie returns to Hell to free Nada, as she told her family she would.
Desire's words would not leave her. Within a week she is standing at the gates of Hell anyway.
A letter arrives, sealed in black wax. Lucifer wishes to see her, and Lucifer does not ask twice.
The last time she came here, she walked past Nada in the ice.
But Hell is empty.
Every cell stands open. Every chain lies slack. The damned, and the demons, are gone.
Only Lucifer remains, alone on his throne, as if he has been waiting for her.

canon: Lucifer has resigned. He has evicted the damned and the demons, and Hell is empty and closing.
He is giving Aurie the key to Hell. If she bested him in his own house before (flag LUCIFER_GRUDGE), he does it to spite her: let her deal with every power that will want it.
He asks one last favour: that she cut off his wings, so he can walk in the mortal world as a man. If she will not, he will do it himself.
Afterwards he will leave for the waking world, free.
conversation.opening: Lady Dream. You came. I have resigned. Hell is closed, the damned are evicted, and I have one last gift for you. And one last favour to ask.
possibilities: She asks why: he says he is tired of being blamed for every sin in creation.
She asks about the favour: he asks her to cut off his wings.
She refuses the key: he drops it at her feet anyway; it is hers now.
suggestions: Why are you giving it to me?
What is the favour?
What will you do now?

exits.4.1.KEY: Aurie takes the key, without helping with his wings.
exits.4.1.WINGS: Aurie takes the key and agrees to cut off Lucifer's wings for him.

choices.text: Give me the key.

aftermath.text: Lucifer takes the knife to his own wings. He does not ask twice.
He walks out into the waking world, a free man, and leaves her holding the key to Hell.
Every power in creation will want it.

choices.text: Give me the key. And the knife. I will help you.

aftermath.text: Aurie cuts. The wings fall away into a storm of feathers.
Lucifer thanks her, which he has never done before, and walks out into the waking world.
Every power in creation will want that key.

4.2.title: The Suitors
4.2.recap: Gods, demons, Faerie and Heaven came to the Dreaming to bid for the key to Hell. Azazel held Nada's soul in a jar.

beats.text: By the time Aurie is home, every realm has heard: the Lady of Dreams holds the key to Hell.
Lucienne is afraid. Whoever holds that key decides what Hell becomes, and every power refused may become an enemy.
So Aurie does what the old laws allow. She invites them all as guests, under her roof, where no guest may harm another.
They come with gifts, and with threats.
Odin All-Father, with Thor and Loki, wanting somewhere to wait out the end of the world.
Azazel, a lord of Hell, who wants his home back. In a jar at his elbow, a captured soul.
It is Nada's soul. When the demons left Hell, Azazel took her with him.
The envoys of Faerie: Cluracan, and his sister Nuala, sent along as a gift.
And two angels, sent by the Creator, who ask for nothing, and only wait.
Before the night is over, Aurie must choose.

conversation.name: The Suitors
canon: Aurie holds the key to Hell and must decide who receives it: the Norse (Odin), Azazel's demons, Faerie (Cluracan), or the angels (Remiel and Duma).
Azazel holds Nada's soul in a jar and threatens to destroy it if Hell is given to anyone else; he offers it in trade for the key.
If the angels receive Hell it becomes a place of redemption, not punishment; the angels never bargain.
Odin wants Hell as a refuge from Ragnarok; Loki whispers clever, dangerous suggestions.
Faerie offers friendship and has brought Nuala as a gift either way.
Every reply is two or three short lines from different suitors, each starting with the speaker's label, like 'ODIN: ... AZAZEL: ...'.
conversation.opening: ODIN: Lady Dream. We have come a long way, and winter is coming for the gods. AZAZEL: Hell is ours by right. Give it back, and I will give you what is in my jar. CLURACAN: Faerie asks only to be your friend, and has brought you a present. REMIEL: We will abide by your decision.
possibilities: She demands Nada's soul from Azazel: he refuses unless he gets the key; the other suitors watch closely.
She asks each what they would do with Hell: they answer in character.
She threatens Azazel: the darkness ripples and the jar's light flickers.
She asks the angels: Remiel says Heaven would make Hell a place where suffering heals.
suggestions: Azazel, give me the soul in that jar.
Odin, why do the gods want Hell?
Remiel, what would Heaven do with it?

exits.4.2.A: Aurie gives the key to the angels.
exits.4.2.B: Aurie gives the key to Odin and the Norse.
exits.4.2.C: Aurie gives the key to Azazel, in exchange for Nada's soul.
exits.4.2.D: Aurie gives the key to Faerie.

choices.text: The key goes to the angels.

Azazel shrieks. The jar cracks, and Nada's soul spills free into Aurie's hands.

choices.text: The key goes to Odin.

aftermath.text: Odin takes the key, and Loki smiles far too widely.
Nada's soul Aurie must buy from Azazel herself. It costs her a dream she loved.

choices.text: Azazel, give me Nada, and the key is yours.

aftermath.text: Azazel opens the jar. Nada is free.
Hell will be worse than it ever was. That is on Aurie now.

choices.text: The key goes to Faerie.

aftermath.text: Cluracan bows extravagantly. Hell will become a wild and strange court.
Nada's soul Aurie takes from Azazel by force, and Faerie stands beside her.

4.3.title: Nada
4.3.recap: Free at last, Nada faced the queen who condemned her.

beats.text: Later, alone, Aurie opens her hand. The small light inside it grows, and becomes a woman.
Nada stands free for the first time in ten thousand years.
She was a queen. She loved Aurie, and refused her, because a mortal who loves one of the Endless brings ruin on her people.
Aurie condemned her to Hell for it.

canon: Nada is free of Hell and stands before Aurie in a white room in the Dreaming.
Ten thousand years ago she refused Aurie's love to save her city, and Aurie condemned her to Hell for it.
If Aurie truly apologises, Nada forgives her and chooses to be reborn into a new mortal life far away.
Nada will not return to Aurie as her lover or queen; she will not be bought.
conversation.opening: So. You freed me. Is this where I thank you, Dream? For ten thousand years in the ice?
possibilities: She apologises sincerely: Nada weeps, and forgives.
She demands Nada come back to her: Nada strikes her.
She offers gifts instead of an apology: Nada refuses them all, coldly.
She asks why Nada refused her: Nada tells her about her city, and the fire.
suggestions: Why did you refuse me?
What do you want now?

exits.4.3.A: Aurie sincerely apologises to Nada and admits she was wrong.
exits.4.3.B: Aurie demands that Nada return to her.
exits.4.3.C: Aurie offers Nada any reward, realm or crown, but no apology.

HEARD_THE_CITY.ripple: For a moment the white room smells of desert smoke.

choices.text: I was wrong. I am sorry, Nada.

aftermath.text: Nada weeps, and forgives her.
She chooses to be born again, far away, into a brand new life.
And Aurie, for the first time in ten thousand years, feels lighter.

choices.text: You are free. Now come back to me.

aftermath.text: Nada strikes her across the face, and walks into the light alone.

choices.text: Ask for anything. A realm, a crown. Anything but that.

aftermath.text: Nada refuses every gift, and leaves without a word.

beats.text: Hell has new masters.
Heaven's angels hold the keys. The damned may heal there now.
Odin's Hell waits for the end of the world. Loki is still smiling.
Azazel's Hell is crueler than it ever was.
Faerie's Hell is a strange, dancing place. Nobody is sure what it is for.
Somewhere in the waking world, a man with no wings plays piano in a bar, and thinks of her kindly.
Nada is gone, born again into a life of her own.
Nada is gone, and she did not forgive.
And Nuala of Faerie stays behind in the Dreaming, a gift to its court, with a favour still to be called.
End of Part Four.

3.0.title: The Mending
3.0.recap: Aurie rebuilt the Dreaming. Then Lucienne brought her a letter from Destiny.

beats.text: With her helm, her sand and her ruby, Aurie begins to rebuild her realm.
The palace rises out of the sand. The gates of horn and ivory close again. Dreams that fled come creeping home.
Aurie walked her sister's rounds. Something of that walk has stayed with her.
Then one evening Lucienne comes to her with a letter, sealed with the sign of a book.
Only one member of her family seals his letters that way.

canon: The Dreaming is being rebuilt. Lucienne has kept the library and the records through it all.
The letter is from Destiny, eldest of the Endless: a summons to a family gathering in his garden tonight. It has not happened in centuries.
The Endless are seven siblings older than the gods: Destiny, Death, Dream (Aurie), Destruction, Desire, Despair and Delirium. Destruction walked away from his duties three hundred years ago.
Lucienne fears Desire will be there; Desire has always enjoyed hurting Aurie.
conversation.opening: My lady. This came for you an hour ago. It carries Destiny's seal. The family is gathering tonight, in his garden.
possibilities: She asks who the Endless are: Lucienne tells her plainly, a line on each, and lingers on Desire.
She asks how the realm is: Lucienne reports with quiet pride, and a little worry.
She does not want to go: Lucienne reminds her that Destiny's summons are never refused.
She confides that she feels changed: Lucienne notices, and is glad.
suggestions: Remind me who my family are.
How is the Dreaming?
Do I have to go?

exits.3.0.GO: Aurie decides to answer Destiny's summons and go.

1.6.title: Paul
1.6.recap: Paul McGuire begged Aurie to lift the curse from Alex.

beats.text: Aurie turns to leave. Paul McGuire is on his knees in the dust, beside the chair.
Fifty years he has loved Alex Burgess. He has never once begged anyone for anything.

canon: It is 1988. Aurie has just cursed Alex Burgess with eternal waking: he will wake from every sleep into a worse nightmare, forever.
Paul McGuire has loved Alex for fifty years. He begs Aurie to lift the curse, and offers to bear it himself.
Alex never hurt Aurie; his father did. Alex was a frightened boy in a cold house who grew into a frightened old man.
Aurie can lift the curse with a gesture, or refuse.
conversation.opening: Please. Please, my lady. He was a frightened boy in a cold house. He never hurt you. Take it off him. Put it on me, if somebody has to pay.
possibilities: She asks why he loves Alex: Paul tells her one small, true thing about him.
She is moved: Paul can hardly believe it.
She is cold: Paul does not stop asking, quietly, until she leaves.
She offers to put the curse on Paul instead: he says yes at once, without a breath.
suggestions: Why do you love him?
Would you really take it for him?

exits.1.6.KEEP: Aurie refuses and leaves the curse in place.

Paul holds him, and weeps, and does not let go.
